sections.html:
Where Mobile Bay begins, the port city of Mobile ranks second in Alabama by population: 187,041 in 2020 and an estimated 204,689 following an annexation in 2023. The land rises from 10 feet along downtown's Water Street to 211 feet near Mobile Regional Airport. Within a few blocks, one house may flood while another stays dry.

Historic districts are plentiful: Ashland Place, Campground, Church Street East, De Tonti Square, Leinkauf, Lower Dauphin Street, Midtown, Oakleigh Garden, Old Dauphin Way, Spring Hill and Toulminville. Houses there often date back a hundred years or longer. Expect questions from a buyer or lender about the roof, wiring, plumbing and foundation, and a repair bill can take a real bite out of a retail sale. A cash buyer who takes the house as is avoids that haggling.

Midtown took the worst of the tornado of December 25, 2012, with damage to at least 100 structures along streets such as Carlen Street, Rickarby Place, Dauphin Street, Old Shell Road and Springhill Avenue.

sections.h2: Who bills the tax and when
sections.html:
Inside city limits, billing and collection belong to the Mobile County Revenue Commission. Offices shut every Wednesday, which means any visit has to be on another weekday.

The October 1 due date is followed by delinquency when December 31 ends. An unpaid account reaches probate court in February, gets advertised in April and can be sold in May.

Totals vary with the school district. The Mobile County Public School System serves most addresses, while Chickasaw, Saraland and Satsuma operate separate systems, so check closely if you live near one of those boundaries.

sections.h2: Water, storms and what buyers check
sections.html:
One 2007 study ranked Mobile the wettest city in the lower 48, averaging 66.3 inches of rain a year. That puts steady strain on roofs, gutters and crawl spaces, with July and August the soggiest months.

Hurricanes are part of local history. Frederic came through in 1979 at Category 3. Opal (1995) and Ivan (2004) caused moderate damage. In 2005 Katrina's 11.45-foot surge put downtown and the elevated Jubilee Parkway underwater. Sally crept through in 2020 as a Category 2, with Zeta arriving a month after.

Heat and humidity matter more than cold to a local inspector, who looks at air conditioning, moisture and mold first. Cash buyers accept storm-damaged or half-repaired houses in their present state, so you need not finish the work before closing.

Deeds are recorded at the county probate office. Under Alabama Code 40-22-1 the recording privilege tax is $0.50 per $500 of value, and a sworn sale price form has to accompany the deed. Leaving the price off or misstating it risks a penalty of $100 or 25% of the tax, whichever is larger. The state receives two thirds of the deed tax and the county one third.

Task at a saleWhere it happens
Pay or clear the current tax balanceUsually at closing, handled by the title company
Sign a deed matching the legal descriptionClosing table
Submit the sale price form with the deedProbate office
Assess the house in the buyer's nameRevenue Commission

To contest an assessed value, go to the county Board of Equalization. If you still disagree with its final decision, Alabama Code 40-3-25 allows 30 days to take the case to circuit court, with notice to the board secretary and circuit clerk plus a bond.

Prior-year taxes must be paid before they go delinquent, or the court may dismiss the case. Stopping payment while you appeal is a good way to lose.

You need not pay the balance beforehand. A title company requests the payoff from the Revenue Commission and deducts it from the proceeds at closing. Get that figure before saying yes to an offer, because it determines what you really keep.

Acting before January keeps the account out of the delinquency process. Come February the file belongs to the probate court, and clearing it costs more.

Most Mobile sellers own an older house, show storm wear and face a tax or probate question. Families in historic neighborhoods often hold a house for decades and then inherit it, and it may sit while an estate is opened. The county's 184,441 housing units in 2020 included 11.2% vacant ones, so empty houses are a visible part of this market.

Cash Home Buyers buys Mobile houses in their present condition, whether tax is due, repairs were put off or a storm left damage. Any balance owed is paid by the title company from proceeds. With no lender appraisal involved, a roof that would fail a mortgage inspection does not kill the deal.

sections.h2: How a sale of a storm-worn house plays out
sections.html:
Begin with a frank list of what is wrong, from the roof and windows to drainage and whatever the last storm left. A financed buyer needs the house to pass an appraisal and usually an insurance review, and storm damage can fail both. A sale that looked solid early on can collapse weeks later for that reason.

A cash sale runs shorter. You send an address and photos, get a written offer, choose a date and sign at the title company. Tax payoff, any older lien and the deed work are handled in that single visit, with no repairs first and no lender to wait on.

sections.h2: What to ask the Revenue Commission
sections.html:
A short call covers most of what a seller needs. Ask what is owed on the parcel today, whether any earlier year is unpaid, and whether an exemption is on file that will need to change when the house sells. Ask too what the office needs to see before it will give a payoff in writing.

Remember that the office is closed on Wednesdays. Calling early in the week leaves time to fix a problem before the title company needs the number, and a written payoff protects you if the closing slips by a few days.

If the house sits near a boundary with Chickasaw, Saraland or Satsuma, confirm which school district and taxing district apply. The answer changes the bill and sometimes surprises owners who assumed otherwise.

Keep notes of each call with the date and the name of the person you spoke with, and save the payoff letter with your closing papers.

Locate three things before you phone anyone: the recorded deed, the newest tax bill and the parcel number. With an inheritance, add papers showing who holds title now. The Revenue Commission can give you the present balance, and the title company can say if a lien from an earlier year is on file.

Copy the legal description off the deed. It must match county records exactly at signing, and a mismatch often delays a closing.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill for a house in Mobile, Alabama?
faqs.a: Billing and collection fall to the Mobile County Revenue Commission, whose offices are closed Wednesdays.

faqs.q: When is property tax due in Mobile?
faqs.a: The due date is October 1 every year and delinquency begins after December 31. An unpaid bill can end up at a May tax sale.
Very. A 2007 study put the yearly average at 66.3 inches, the highest of any city in the contiguous 48 states.

faqs.q: What is the deed tax on a Mobile house sale?
faqs.a: The rate is $0.50 per $500 of value under Alabama Code 40-22-1, and the deed needs an attached form stating the actual sale price.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Mobile house if it has hurricane damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers purchase hurricane-damaged houses as they are, and unpaid tax is taken from the closing proceeds.
